Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form + MSA redline: data & output rights

Grace —

Thanks for the call earlier. We've attached a redlined version of the order form and a few MSA excerpts that we need clarified before we can move to procurement. High-level asks from Legal/Privacy: 

- Customers must retain title to any output generated from their data (explicit "title to output" clause).
- Atlas requires a formal opt-out from model training: if Redwood uses customer data or outputs to improve models, customer must explicitly consent — otherwise no training.
- Feedback license: any telemetry/feedback that Redwood uses for product improvements must be anonymized and not tied back to Atlas data, or we require a limited license with a termination right.

We redlined suggested language in the attached doc (Atlas_OrderForm_Redline_20280320.docx). Please confirm Redwood's position in writing, and if you think this needs legal call, propose times this week. Procurement hopes to get an executable order form by the end of the month.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Director, Cloud Integrations
Atlas Systems

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form + MSA redline: data & output rights

Sanjay —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redline. I'm looping in our contracts & product leads to get a short position and a proposed compromise.

Initial thoughts: 
- Title to customer output is something we can reasonably accommodate as long as the scope is limited to the customer-produced prompts and direct outputs; we usually exclude model-level parameters/weights and improvements derived from aggregated signals.
- Training opt-out is possible but has operational and pricing implications — customers who opt out from training typically require a dedicated model variant or an annual fee to offset reduced improvement across the shared model.
- For feedback/telemetry, we can commit to using only aggregated, non-identifiable signals for product telemetry by default, and provide a more restrictive IP license if Atlas requires.

I'll coordinate a short legal call tomorrow with our Legal (Laura) and Sales Ops (Ben/Karthik). Does 3pm PT tomorrow work for you?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
AM, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Folks —

Forwarding Atlas's redline. Summary of proposed internal position (draft):

1) Output ownership: We accept customer title to "Customer Outputs" defined as (i) prompts submitted by the customer, (ii) resulting text/images/videos produced in response, and (iii) any customer-provided files. We carve out: model parameters, aggregated model improvements, and Redwood-owned system prompts. Suggested language: "Customer shall retain title to Customer Outputs subject to Redwood's right to use Aggregated Feedback as set forth below."

2) Training opt-out: Offer two paths: 
   a) Standard: customer consents to non-identifiable, aggregated training data use (no PII).
   b) Opt-out: customer can opt out of training; opt-out triggers either (i) a 15% uplift on the annual order value, or (ii) placement on a Dedicated/Isolated model at additional cost.

3) Feedback/Telemetry: Commit to use Aggregated Feedback for product improvements. If Atlas requires a stricter feedback license (no use for model training or product improvements), Legal suggests a limited license term (e.g., 12 months) with explicit scope and an audit right.

Attachments: redline_summary_Grace-20280322.xlsx (high-level impact matrix).

Next steps: Laura, can you convert the above into concrete clauses we can propose to Atlas? Grace, if Atlas accepts the pricing uplift or dedicated model route we can fast-track procurement.

- Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 24 Mar 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order Form + MSA redline: data & output rights

Team —

I've drafted redline language attached (proposed_msa_excerpt_20280324.docx) and a short rationale below. High-level position we can take without opening broad precedents: 

A) Customer Outputs / Title
Proposed clause: "Customer shall retain title to Customer Outputs (as defined) and Redwood shall have a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free right to use Customer Outputs only to provide the Services to Customer and to maintain security, and otherwise only as Aggregated Feedback subject to the Feedback License below."

B) Aggregated Feedback and Telemetry
Proposed clause: "Aggregated Feedback means statistical or other de-identified information derived from Customer Outputs that cannot be traced back to Customer or any individual. Redwood may use Aggregated Feedback to develop, improve and operate the Services. Redwood will not use Customer Outputs to retrain the Customer's dedicated model without express written consent."

C) Training Opt-Out
Option 1 (no opt-out fee): Allow opt-out but require customer to accept limited product-level SLA and possible feature lag. Not recommended.
Option 2 (recommended): Provide explicit opt-out election for model training; if elected, Customer will pay an Opt-Out Fee (we propose 15% of MRR or a fixed annual add-on) or transition to a Dedicated/Private deployment with associated fees. This preserves product economics.

D) Audit / Escrow / Termination Rights
If Atlas insists on a very restrictive feedback license, we should limit the term (e.g., 12 months) and require an audit trigger with defined scope and cost recovery. 

I recommend we present Option 2 to Atlas (opt-out + fee or dedicated). It is commercially reasonable and keeps model improvements viable. I've included tracked redlines for the MSA excerpts; see Attachment.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_msa_excerpt_20280324.docx

Grace / Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear choices. After internal review, Atlas is comfortable with the proposed compromise: 

- Atlas retains title to Customer Outputs as defined.
- Atlas will take the Opt-Out election for training in the initial 12-month term and accept the proposed Opt-Out Fee (we agree to the 15% uplift for year one).
- Atlas requires a 12-month limited feedback license (no model retraining on Atlas data) and agrees to the audit process outlined if needed.

Procurement will prepare the PO once we have the finalized order form and the MSA excerpt integrated. Can Redwood send a clean order form and a single-page summary of the concessions so our procurement and legal execs can sign off? Also please include the DocuSign link for countersignature.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Sanjay Rao
